body: Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services (owned by LIC, SBI, ORIX, ADIA, HDFC) had ~Rs 91,000 cr group debt across 300+ subsidiaries by Mar 2018 and AAA ratings on some paper until early Aug 2018. First default came at subsidiary IL&FS Transportation (ITNL) in Jun 2018 (~Rs 450 cr ICDs/CP); ICRA cut AAA to AA+ in Jul; the parent defaulted on a Rs 1,000 cr SIDBI loan on 4 Sep 2018; within days ratings went AAA -> D. The government superseded the board on 1 Oct 2018 (Uday Kotak-led). Listed subsidiaries ITNL and IL&FS Engineering fell >90%. The default froze India's CP market and triggered the NBFC crisis (DHFL, Reliance Capital, Altico). Visible flags: (1) consolidated interest coverage near/below 1x -- operating cash flow did not cover interest; (2) long-gestation road/power projects funded with short debt and constant refinancing; (3) 300+ subsidiaries/cross-guarantees made consolidated leverage opaque; (4) ratings leaned on 'parentage' (LIC/SBI) not standalone cash; (5) listed ITNL showed rising debt, receivables from government authorities and claims-based 'income'. Lesson: AAA is not a cash-flow test; a holding structure that needs perpetual refinancing fails the day markets close; rating agency downgrades are lagging.

data.early_signals: interest coverage <1; refinancing dependence; complex group structure; first sub default Jun 2018
data.lesson: Compute interest cover and refinancing needs yourself; parentage-based ratings lag
data.spotted_by: few; ICRA July 2018 note was late

title: IL&FS default: AAA-rated group that couldn't pay (2018)
